text:
Leah K: noticed unusual node-level rolebinding created in cluster-alpha, looks like it grants `gpu-pool-access` to `system:node-proxy`
Samir P: who created it? any deploys around that ts?
Leah K: checked deploy history — nothing obvious. `kubectl get clusterrolebinding gpu-node-proxy -o yaml` shows a `subjects` entry with kind: Group name: system:nodes
Maria G: that sounds like propagation from a misconfigured RoleBinding -> ClusterRoleBinding sync job we've been trying to lock down
Owen R: pinging audit logs now, will grep for the API server `create` event
audit-bot: audit log match: 1975432053 | user: deploy-controller | sourceIPs: 10.120.0.5 | requestURI: "/apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/clusterrolebindings"
Samir P: deploy-controller? that service account shouldn't have cluster role create rights anymore after the least-privilege PR
Leah K: exact. suspect a rollback of the controller image to an older tag that still had broad perms
Maria G: can we confirm with `kubectl auth can-i create clusterrolebinding --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:deploy-controller` ?
Owen R: ran it: `no` now. but the audit log shows it succeeded at 1975432053
Leah K: we need to snapshot the clusterrolebinding and revoke it quickly if still present. also rotate any KMS keys that svc acct might have used to encrypt temp creds (just in case)
Samir P: removing binding now: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding gpu-node-proxy` — queued, will report back
Leah K: good. also mark this as incident, create ticket, and add short mitigation steps for oncall
oncall-engr: acknowledged, creating INC-2026-134 in jira with tags: security, rbac, gpu
Maria G: patch suggestion: make the clusterrolebinding controller explicitly ignore `system:nodes` group and gate creation behind a feature flag + an audit webhook that rejects cluster-wide elevation ops from deploy-controller image older than sha X
Samir P: we should also add an automated check in CI: fail PRs that reintroduce clusterrolebinding creation into deploy-controller manifests
Owen R: found another audit line showing decrypt to KMS: `kms.decrypt` by serviceaccount infra/deploy-controller at 1975432060 — suggests it used encrypted creds for the op
Leah K: action items: 1) rotate KMS key used by deploy-controller 2) revoke and delete gpu-node-proxy binding 3) block deploy-controller image tag < sha on admission 4) postmortem in 48h
Maria G: adding note: verify no pods got GPU annotation while binding existed — run `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["redwood/gpu-access"]=="true")'`
Samir P: delete command succeeded, binding gone. audit shows delete by Samir at 1975432170
Leah K: great. please attach audit export and any affected pod list to the jira ticket. cc @security@redwood.com
Owen R: will export and push to secure S3; sharing link in ticket
Maria G: if we confirm no lateral access, consider this an elevated-risk misconfig but not breached. still run full creds rotation for affected svc acct
Leah K: agreed. I'll draft the postmortem template and assign owners for follow-ups. thanks everyone :lock:
Samir P: learning: rolebinding -> clusterrolebinding propagation edge-case is subtle, we'll add unit tests for the controller to simulate node groups
oncall-engr: incident created and pager cleared
